text:
Benchmarks rose over 1.5% on Tuesday as the Finance Minister said she would welcome views on LTCG tax and STT.

• Sensex closed at 73,033.78, up 1,109.10 points (1.54%); Nifty 50 closed at 22,721.95, up 358.60 points (1.60%), per Business Standard and HDFC Sky closing reports.
• Nifty IT rose about 5.2%, the top sectoral gainer, after HCLTech reported a 21.2% year-on-year rise in September-quarter net profit (per HDFC Sky).
• Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said it is healthy to have a debate on long-term capital gains tax and that she would be keen to hear views (per Upstox and Business Standard). No formal proposal has been announced.
• Foreign investors were reported to have sold Indian shares for a 12th straight session on Monday (per HDFC Sky).

Our view: markets often react quickly to any hint of a change in tax treatment, but a willingness to hear views is not a policy change. Today's move also had other contributors, including IT earnings and softer crude, so we would not attribute it to a single cause. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: when tax-policy debates move markets, how do you help clients separate headline noise from decisions that actually affect their long-term plans?
